claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs: 'You can use workload resources to create and manage multiple Pods for you. A controller for the resource handles replication and rollout and automatic healing in case of Pod failure.' Execution (outputs/stage-2/scripts/k8s/replicaset.txt, server v1.34.11): after 'kubectl delete pod web', 'kubectl get pod web' -> 'Error from server (NotFound): pods "web" not found'.

'A ReplicaSet is defined with fields, including a selector that specifies how to identify Pods it can acquire, a number of replicas indicating how many Pods it should be maintaining, and a pod template specifying the data of new Pods it should create ... A ReplicaSet then fulfills its purpose by creating and deleting Pods as needed to reach the desired number. When a ReplicaSet needs to create new Pods, it uses its Pod template.'

controller.md: 'Kubernetes comes with a set of built-in controllers that run inside the kube-controller-manager.' 'Built-in controllers manage state by interacting with the cluster API server.' glossary/controller.md: 'A control loop that watches the shared state of the cluster through the apiserver and makes changes...' kubernetes-api.md: 'Users, the different parts of your cluster, and external components all communicate with one another through the API server.' components.md lists kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler under Control Plane.

'The .spec.template is a Pod template. It has exactly the same schema as a Pod, except it is nested and does not have an apiVersion or kind.' (deployment.md; same sentence in replicationcontroller.md; replicaset.md: '.spec.template is a pod template which is also required to have labels in place').
